newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi hopes for rapid metalworkers' deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi hopes for rapid metalworkers' deal.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi hopes talks resuming on Monday between employers and unions in Italy's engineering and metalworking industry will yield a rapid resolution to their pay dispute, a government statement said.

The statement was issued after Prodi met leaders of the country's three main labour confederations, CGIL, CISL and UIL and the Italian employers' group Confindustria to encourage the search for a deal.

"At the end of the meeting, by common agreement, it was decided to resume talks immediately among the parties at the Labour Ministry in order to reach a rapid conclusion to the dispute," the statement said.
The talks, the first in months, are between the industry group Federmeccanica and sectoral unions FIOM, FIM and UILM.

The protracted dispute, which has been accompanied by three one-day strikes since it began six months ago, affects 1.7 million workers in a sector which accounts for 40 percent of Italy's industrial output.
Any deal is likely to set the tone for other pay settlements and prove key to Italy's hopes of keeping a lid on inflation.
